summary: Enable Slack-driven Jira issue creation workflow with approval gateway and audit tags
description:
Issue summary: Request to enable a Slack-first path for oncall and ops teams to create Jira support issues via a controlled approval gateway. The flow should create a minimal Jira ticket, attach audit tags, and only escalate to full support workflow after approval from an approver group.

Impact: Currently, oncall-runbooks and SREs escalate via manual Jira creation or post to #support which creates noise. This automation will reduce mean time to acknowledge for urgent ops items while preserving auditability and preventing accidental ticket sprawl. Expected to reduce manual create time for runbook escalations by ~40%.

Background: We have several one-off Slack shortcuts that post to channels, but they create unstructured messages. Previous attempts to auto-create Jira issues caused duplicate/low-quality tickets and lacked an approval gate and audit metadata. This request ties into existing runbook provisioning (see linked issues) and the audit tagging standard.

Requirements:
- Slack shortcut /slash command that collects minimal fields (title, severity, short description, optional runbook link).
- Present an approver modal to on-call rotation group (with configurable timeout).
- On approval: create full Jira issue with labels and custom audit fields, add link back to Slack thread, and post an acknowledgement message.
- On timeout/deny: create a lightweight ephemeral note in a private ops channel and mark request as declined in Jira.
- All created issues must include: origin=slack_gateway, requester=current_user, approver_group, audit_tags (data_class, prod_impact).
- Admin console page (Confluence) listing approver groups and escalation timeouts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Manual test: run through creation and approval flows end-to-end in prod workspace without creating duplicate tickets.
- Automation: Gateway respects RBAC group membership; non-approvers cannot escalate without secondary approval.
- Audit: Every Jira created has audit_tags populated and a Confluence page documents flows and admin steps.

Steps to reproduce (manual test):
1) In #oncall-runbook channel, invoke /create-support (shortcut) and fill form.
2) Approver receives modal and approves.
3) Verify Jira issue created with correct fields and links.
4) Verify Slack thread updated and Confluence admin page lists the event.

Example logs / payload samples:
- Slack interaction payload sample: <redacted payload> (stored in ops-artifacts/645210/slack-payload.json).
- Jira create API call: POST /rest/api/2/issue -> returns 201 with key and issue link.

Notes: This will touch the slack-bot service, Jira webhook handlers, and Confluence documentation automation. Consider rate-limiting and idempotency keys for retries.

Ethan Cho (2026-03-12): Spike complete. Prototype posts to a staging project OK; found two failure modes: duplicate submissions when approver modal resubmits, and missing audit_tags when Jira project mapping omitted a field. Plan: add idempotency token and validation hook in webhook handler. Creating follow-up subtasks for mapping cleanup.
Marisol Vega (2026-03-12): Thanks — please add a short runbook snippet in Confluence for emergency bypass and document the approver group membership process.
investigation_notes: Spike run results: prototype uses a temporary idempotency-key stored in redis; works in staging but needs TTL tuning.

Observed duplicate issue creation when Slack modal closed and reopened quickly; likely due to frontend firing multiple interaction payloads. Recommended debounce client-side plus server-side idempotency check.
Jira mapping issue: custom field 'audit_tags' not present in PROD support project. Created INT-645211 to request field creation and mapping cleanup.
RBAC: approver group membership is sourced from SCIM-managed Okta group 'ops-approvers'. Confirm synchronization schedule with Identity team.
workaround: Until automation is live, oncall should use the /create-jira shortcut which opens a prefilled Jira issue in browser. For urgent items, mention @ops-approvers in the channel to request manual approval.
